qualitative.gate_2_reason: Commodity price taker lacking pricing power in undifferentiated natural gas upstream exploration and production.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (REJECT – G2 Essential Need). Pure commodity price-taker lacking pricing power in natural gas upstream exploration and production. While natural gas provides essential heating and electricity generation, EQT produces an undifferentiated commodity sold at volatile NYMEX Henry Hub spot prices with zero pricing power. Even with the Equitrans Midstream integration lowering gathering costs and adding Mountain Valley Pipeline assets, multi-cycle GAAP ROIC is ~6.8% (well below the 12% moat hurdle) and cash flows remain hostage to commodity boom-and-bust cycles.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 6.8%, well below the 12% compounder hurdle. Performance is driven by volatile commodity pricing rather than compounding: FY24 revenue was $5.27B with operating income of $685M (13.0% margin), net income of $231M, FCF attributable to EQT of ~$684M, and ROIC of ~1.28%. FY25 rebounded with revenue of $8.64B, operating income of $3.25B (37.6% margin), net income of $2.04B, FCF of ~$2.50B, and ROIC of ~5.79% (external tax-effected NOPAT ROIC ~9-10%). Closed acquisition of Equitrans Midstream in July 2024 for enterprise value >$35B, reintegrating 2,000+ miles of gathering pipelines and the Mountain Valley Pipeline (MVP) to lower unlevered FCF breakeven to ~$2.00/MMBtu. However, EQT remains an upstream price-taker with >80% of revenue derived from wholesale natural gas sales with zero pricing power over inflation. Total debt spiked to ~$14B post-merger in mid-2024 before being reduced to ~$7.8B by year-end 2025 via merger cash flows and non-core asset sales.
